entries.text: GSQ (Gumbel-Softmax Quantization) learns better rounding at 2 to 3 bits. RCO (Riemannian Constrained Optimization) picks a type per tensor so the file hits an exact size. Some community repos reuse the tag without being part of ISTA.

entries.title: E2B: Google Gemma "effective" parameters
entries.text: Google Gemma "effective" parameters. The model also has large per-layer embedding tables that are looked up rather than computed, so E4B is about 8B in total and the file is bigger than "4B" suggests.

entries.title: 35B-A3B: Mixture of experts (MoE)
entries.text: Mixture of experts (MoE). The first number is total parameters and the second is the parameters active per token. You need memory for the total. Speed follows the active count.

entries.title: MoE: Mixture of experts
entries.text: Mixture of experts. A router sends each token to a few of many "expert" sub-networks.

entries.title: 8X3B-MOE: Eight separate dense 3B models joined with a router using MergeKit (DavidAU)
entries.text: Eight separate dense 3B models joined with a router using MergeKit (DavidAU). They were not trained together like a native MoE.

entries.title: 24GB: Memory budgets
entries.text: Memory budgets. NVIDIA's 74B-A9B-24GB is designed to fit under 24 GB. The 16GB repo is a community build that removes half the experts. The meaning of 4GB on the E4B repo is not stated.

entries.title: 152E: Keeps 152 of 288 experts per layer, chosen with RCO (expert pruning)
entries.text: Keeps 152 of 288 experts per layer, chosen with RCO (expert pruning).

entries.text: Parameters were removed to shrink the model.

entries.text: REINFORCE Leave-One-Out, a reinforcement learning method from Cohere. Each answer is scored against the average of the other answers to the same prompt.

entries.title: DPO: Direct Preference Optimization
entries.text: Direct Preference Optimization. Training on pairs of preferred and rejected answers. SimPO is a variant.

entries.title: LoRA: small add-on to a base model
entries.text: Low-Rank Adaptation. A small add-on that changes what a base model does. It cannot run on its own: load it with the base model it was trained for.

entries.title: QAT: Quantization-aware training
entries.text: Quantization-aware training. The model is trained while simulating low-bit weights, so a later 4-bit quant loses very little.

entries.title: QAD: Quantization-aware distillation
entries.text: Quantization-aware distillation. Similar to QAT, used by NVIDIA and Liquid AI.

entries.title: Fusion: DavidAU's own training recipes, not merges (author label)
entries.text: DavidAU's own training recipes, not merges (author label). Numbers like 735 are benchmark scores.

entries.title: abliterated: Refusals removed by editing weights
entries.text: Refusals removed by editing weights. The method finds the "refusal direction" in the model's activations and removes it from the weights. It comes from the 2024 research by Arditi, Nanda and others, and FailSpy's abliterator library. huihui-ai publishes many of these.

entries.title: Heretic: Made with p-e-w's Heretic tool
entries.text: Made with p-e-w's Heretic tool. It automatically tunes the abliteration so the model refuses less while changing as little as possible (low KL divergence).

entries.title: OBLITERATED: Made with Pliny the Prompter's OBLITERATUS toolkit, which removes refusal directions in several passes
entries.text: Made with Pliny the Prompter's OBLITERATUS toolkit, which removes refusal directions in several passes.

entries.title: Uncensored: A general claim that the model refuses less
entries.text: A general claim that the model refuses less. It does not name a method. Read the model card.

entries.title: dealignai: An uploader whose releases are weight-level abliteration only
entries.text: An uploader whose releases are weight-level abliteration only.

entries.title: Aggressive: HauhauCS's two strengths
entries.text: HauhauCS's two strengths. Balanced is the recommended default. Aggressive is for cases where Balanced still refuses. The method is not published.

entries.title: MTP: Multi-token prediction
entries.text: Multi-token prediction. Extra layers, trained with the model, that guess the next few tokens. Qwen3.8 and DeepSeek ship them. -MTP in a repo name means the GGUF keeps these tensors (many converters drop them). In llama.cpp, turn it on with --spec-type draft-mtp (added May 2026). The author of that feature reported more than 2 times faster generation, and other users reported 1.7 to 1.9 times.

entries.title: Native-MTP-Preserved: The uncensored model still has all of its original MTP tensors
entries.text: The uncensored model still has all of its original MTP tensors.

entries.title: K-quant mix size
entries.text: _S, _M and _L are small, medium and large mixes of the same base type. A bigger mix gives more bits to the tensors that hurt quality most when rounded. Q3_K, Q4_K and Q5_K alone are aliases for the _M versions.

entries.title: Effective parameters
entries.text: Google Gemma effective parameters. The file is bigger than the number suggests because of the large per-layer embedding tables.

entries.text: Total parameters, then the parameters active per token. You need memory for the total. Speed follows the active number.

entries.title: Parameter count
entries.text: Billions of parameters. Memory for weights is about this number times bits per weight divided by 8, in GB.

entries.title: XL mix size
entries.text: _XL is a size label for a larger mix of a K-quant, not a llama.cpp type. With the UD- prefix it is Unsloth's own label, which Unsloth does not define in its docs. On bartowski files (Q3_K_XL, Q6_K_L style) it means the standard quant with the embedding and output weights at Q8_0.

entries.title: W#A#: weight and activation bits
entries.text: W is the number of bits used to store the weights. A is the number of bits used for the activations, the values passed between layers, during the math. The label does not say which tool loads the file: ComfyUI and vLLM models both use it, and it may need a specific loader. A trailing s is a plural.

entries.title: MXFP#: MX floating point
entries.text: Microscaling floating-point weights at the stated number of bits. Check config.json for the activation width.

entries.title: INT#: integer weights
entries.text: Usually integer weights at the stated number of bits. Check config.json to be sure.
